newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon bombs kill civilian, wound guerrilla.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon bombs kill civilian, wound guerrilla.

text.p: A Lebanese villager was killed and a Hizbollah guerrilla was wounded on Wednesday when four roadside bombs exploded near their pickup truck in the eastern Bekaa valley close to Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, security sources said.
"The 22-year-old wounded man is a Hizbollah guerrilla. He was injured by shrapnels which hit different parts of his body. He is in hospital," a security source told Reuters.
The source named the man as Ali Ahmed, son-in-law of the villager and brother of a Hizbollah senior official -- all from the village of Zillaya, on the edge of the zone.
"Kamal Ahmed, the brother of Ali, is a high-ranking official at Hizbollah. Kamal's wife and his father were martyred in an Israeli air raid on Zillaya a few years ago," the source added.
"His second brother Mohammed Ahmed was a Hizbollah guerrilla who martyred during a guerrilla attack against Israeli targets in Zomrayya in 1990," the source added.

A Hizbollah spokesman issued a statement saying Israeli forces detonated the four bombs by remote control. The pro-Iranian group is fighting to drive Israel and its local militia allies from the south.

Anti-Israeli Moslem guerrillas and Israeli troops frequently plant roadside bombs in south Lebanon in attempts to ambush each other. Many Shi'ite Moslem villagers are believed to be involved in guerrilla operations against the Israelis.
